description: Generated from canonical role-based Markdown; no automatic truth, causal, symmetric or transitive inference.

nodes.label: The same prominent word can participate in a narrow focus or a larger focused constituent.
An affix is a bound morphological element attached to a base in the analysis adopted here.
Allomorphy is variation in the forms realizing a morphological unit.
Ambiguity involves distinguishable interpretations of a form or structure.
Produce a multi-level analysis whose representations remain distinct and whose interfaces are explicit.
Record candidate constituent boundaries and local relations using converging diagnostics.
Distinguish morphological exponents, phonological categories and observed phonetic realizations.
Anaphora links an expression's interpretation to discourse material or a structurally available antecedent.
A prosodic investigation should keep interpretive labels, annotation decisions and acoustic measurements separate while linking each result to an identifiable recording and context.
English auxiliary constructions constrain the form of a following verb.
Local auxiliary selection explains the form of each following verb independently of the construction label.
A syntactic category classifies an expression by its structural and distributional properties; a grammatical function describes its relationship within a larger construction.
A category label does not uniquely determine the grammatical function of its instances.
Identify what the input represents, build a justified articulatory description, then listen and attempt the sound without confusing a chart label, a phoneme or an observed token.
The working clause representation distinguishes Subject from Predicate and then analyzes the predicate's head, complements and modifiers.
Cohesion concerns linguistic linking devices such as reference chains, repetition, lexical relations, ellipsis and connectives.
Explicit linguistic links do not by themselves establish a well motivated conceptual relationship among all discourse units.
Collocation concerns conventional patterns of lexical co-occurrence.
Common ground is information participants mutually treat as accepted for the purposes of an interaction in a working discourse model.
Separate participant roles from grammatical functions when comparing constructions.
A complement is licensed by the relevant head or construction in a closer selectional relationship; a modifier contributes a less lexically restricted elaboration.
A complement clause occupies a position licensed by a head or construction.
The compositionality principle relates the interpretation of a complex expression to interpretations of its parts and their mode of combination.
Compounding combines lexical bases into a larger lexical expression.
Connected-speech processes describe context-sensitive realization across segments and word boundaries.
Consonants can be classified by voicing, place and manner of articulation.
A constituent is a unit in a proposed hierarchical syntactic analysis.
A grammatical licensing condition concerns what a stated grammar permits.
Conventional meaning can constrain reference without uniquely determining the referent of an utterance.
Contextual resolution identifies values needed to interpret an expression in its use, such as a pronoun referent, deictic place or relevant comparison class.
Contrast presents a relevant difference or opposition between discourse units.
A minimal pair differs in one relevant segment while contrasting lexical identity.
Coordination combines expressions of comparable syntactic status; subordination makes a clause dependent within a larger structure.
Deictic expressions anchor interpretation to features of an utterance context such as speaker, addressee, place or time.
Derivation forms a related lexeme using a morphological pattern.
Dialogue is jointly organized through turns, responses and repair, so an utterance's contribution depends partly on its position in an interaction.
A stated discourse context constrains an information-structure analysis without making grammatical Subject, Topic and Focus interchangeable.
A discourse model tracks referents and relations while keeping textual order distinct from event order and causal direction.
A discourse referent is a representation used to track an individual, group, event or other object through discourse.
A discourse relation links units through an interpretive relation such as explanation, result, elaboration, example, contrast or condition.
Ordinary English main-clause interrogatives and sentential negation interact with auxiliary syntax.
An English analysis may require understood but unpronounced material or dependencies whose related elements are not adjacent, so surface contiguity is not a universal guide to structure.
English is documented here through distinct, interacting representations rather than a fixed processing staircase.
Assess a bounded claim against inspected sources, counterexamples and its declared scope before changing evidence status.
An attested token, a constructed example, an elicited judgment, a source statement and an analyst's model are different evidence objects.
Regular English plural and past endings vary with the relevant final sound of the base rather than its last written letter.
A linguistic expression and an analysis of it are different objects.
Finiteness classifies a clause or verbal element relative to tense, agreement and distributional properties in a particular grammar.
Focus domains constrain possible prosodic realizations without being identical to the most strongly accented word.
Topic concerns what a discourse stretch is about; a question under discussion is the issue being addressed; focus relates an expression or domain to relevant alternatives.
A Subject need not be an Agent, and an Object need not be a Patient.
Givenness concerns contextual accessibility, not a permanent lexical property.
Grammaticality concerns licensing under a specified grammar or variety.
Gricean analysis models conversational expectations involving informativeness, truthfulness or support, relevance and clarity.
A head is the organizing element of a headed construction in a stated analysis.
Conversational implicature concerns communicated information beyond what is straightforwardly asserted under the relevant conventional interpretation.
A context-supported inference can be cancelled without cancelling the asserted existential content that supported it.
Inflection realizes grammatical distinctions within a lexeme's paradigm in the working lexeme-based model.
English constructions can package similar propositional material differently by changing which material is presented as prominent, presupposed, topical or contrastive.
A worked passage illustrates parallel analyses across subsystems while distinguishing explicit claims from contextual preferences.
An interface is a systematic correspondence or constraint between representations in different analytical systems.
Turn a bounded English question into a transparent provisional analysis and a reviewable evidence trail.
Learn one General American word by connecting its intended meaning, checked phonemic form, listening evidence, articulatory actions, recorded attempts and a later unprompted check.
A lexeme is an abstract lexical identity associated with a family of grammatical forms.
A lexical entry represents item-specific linguistic information relevant to a lexeme or sense: form, category, paradigm, meaning, selection, alternations and conventional combinations.
Lexical items and senses can stand in relations such as hyponymy, incompatibility, synonymy and opposition, but these relations apply to specified senses rather than spellings in isolation.
Selection relates lexical senses and constructions to allowable complements and their semantic properties.
English lexical choices vary across communities, situations, genres and historical periods, so a lexical entry must not be treated as uniform across all speakers and contexts.
Lexical entries and morphological structure constrain one another without reducing every word form or derived word to an independently listed spelling.
A sense-specific lexical entry constrains an interpretation without making a spelling identify one context-independent predicate.
Lexical senses and constructions constrain the category and form of licensed syntactic complements.
A relation between an inner NP and its preposition must be distinguished from the relation between the whole PP and a higher head.
Review changes and publish a coherent provisional package without confusing file integrity with linguistic truth.
Modality evaluates possibilities or necessities relative to a source of constraints and, in many theories, an ordering of relevant alternatives.
A morpheme is an abstract unit associated with a recurring grammatical or lexical contribution in a morphological analysis.
Regular English inflection links morphological features to sound-conditioned exponents.
Word-form features and syntactic distributions must be represented separately even when an analysis connects them through agreement or finiteness.
Under a stated classical interpretation, P entails Q if every model making P true makes Q true.
A clause analysis records complete constituent spans and their nesting rather than counting verb-looking tokens.
A Direct Object and a PP complement are different syntactic realizations.
A paradigm organizes the grammatical forms of a lexeme by feature values or form categories.
A phoneme is an abstract contrastive category in a language analysis.
A phonological analysis depends on representational and theoretical choices, so the same pattern may receive competing feature, rule, constraint or usage-based accounts.
Segment categories, syllable organization, stress and phonetic realization provide distinct descriptions of a sound pattern.
Phonological representations constrain possible phonetic analyses without uniquely specifying an observed speech token.
Phonotactics concerns restrictions and preferences on segment distributions and combinations in a language or variety.
A phrase is a syntactic unit organized as a phrase category; it may contain one word or many.
Plural expressions can support distributive, collective and cumulative interpretations, so grammatical plurality does not uniquely determine how a predicate applies to participants.
Utterance design can manage social relationships and identities, but politeness and social meaning depend on community norms, activity and participant interpretation rather than fixed word lists.
Contextual interpretation updates an evolving discourse model, while that discourse model in turn constrains later reference and inference.
A predicative complement attributes a property, classification or identity to a predicand rather than functioning as an ordinary Object participant.
A presupposition is content treated as backgrounded in a use or associated with a triggering construction in a theory.
Productivity concerns the extendability of a pattern to suitable new bases.
Prosody organizes prominence, pitch patterns, timing and phrasing beyond individual segment identities.
A prosodic prominence analysis must be distinguished from the phonetic measurements used to investigate its realization.
Quantification specifies how a claim ranges over a contextually relevant domain.
A finite-domain toy model makes scope differences explicit without claiming that logic alone predicts English reading availability.
A phonological category can have different phonetic realizations without a change of lexical identity.
Reference concerns what an expression is used to pick out in context; denotation is a semantic value under an interpretation.
An integrated relative clause modifies a nominal expression and establishes a dependency involving a position within that clause.
Orthography describes writing; phonology describes language-specific sound organization; phonetics describes speech production, signals and perception.
A root is a minimally analyzable lexical core within the chosen morphological analysis.
Reversing quantifier or negation scope can change truth conditions while leaving overt words in the same order.
Knowing a word's lexical category alone does not determine all of its allowable complement patterns.
A semantic predicate expresses a property or relation that combines with arguments.
A semantic role characterizes a participant's relationship to a predicate or situation.
Conventional meaning, contextual resolution and defeasible inference jointly constrain utterance interpretation.
A sense is a conventional interpretation associated with a lexical item in an analysis.
An event following another in time does not by itself demonstrate that the earlier event caused it.
Situation type concerns a predicate or construction's temporal and dynamic character.
A speech act is a communicative action performed through an utterance, such as asserting, asking, requesting or promising.
Lexical stress is a prominence relation among syllables in a word.
Suppletion describes paradigm-related forms whose relationship is not a regular productive phonological alternation in the synchronic system.
A working syllable model divides a syllable into onset and rhyme, with nucleus and coda inside the rhyme.
Syntactic structure constrains prosodic phrasing, but prosodic boundaries need not reproduce every syntactic constituent boundary one for one.
Construction-sensitive mappings connect grammatical functions with semantic roles without identifying the two dimensions.
Temporal relations locate situations before, after or overlapping others.
Temporal interpretation separates tense, reference time, event structure and aspectual viewpoint.
Tense relates temporal reference to an evaluation context; aspect concerns temporal perspective and situation structure.
Track reference and discourse relations while distinguishing asserted information from defeasible inference.
A sentence is a linguistic expression considered abstractly; an utterance is a particular use in context.
An utterance interpretation records conventional constraints, contextual values and defeasible communicated inferences separately.
Valency describes a head's capacity for core arguments; argument structure represents the associated participant relations.
Passing publication checks establishes only the properties those checks actually inspect.
Vowel descriptions commonly use height, backness and lip rounding.
A wh-dependency links an interrogative or relative expression with a grammatical position in a clause.
Morphological analyses distinguish the element, the operation, its input base and the resulting lexeme or word form.
An accented word need not exhaust the focus domain
Category does not determine grammatical function
Cohesive links do not guarantee coherence
Context supplies values for context sensitive expressions
Regular inflectional exponents are conditioned by stem sounds
Focus topic and question under discussion
Grammatical functions do not determine semantic roles
Local heads determine local dependency relations
Scope determines the interaction of semantic operators
Complement selection is sensitive to lexical sense and construction
Temporal sequence does not establish causation
Structural validation does not establish linguistic truth
